key_insight: LoL identifies a critical failure mode called sink-collapse—where generated video repeatedly reverts to an attention "sink" frame—and introduces sink-robust modeling and training strategies that preserve coherence to scale autoregressive video generation to hour-long outputs.
problem_solved: Addresses error accumulation and loss of long-term temporal coherence in autoregressive long-form video generation, specifically preventing abrupt scene resets and cyclic motion patterns caused by attention sink frames.
method: Diagnose sink-collapse and modify attention dynamics to reduce over-reliance on sink frames (sink-aware / sink-robust attention mechanisms and gating).
Introduce temporal consistency objectives and hierarchical memory / context-refresh strategies to preserve long-range dependencies while keeping computation efficient.
Use training curricula and overlapping-chunk generation to stabilize autoregressive sampling for hour-scale outputs.
impact: Makes autoregressive video models practical for hour-scale generation with fewer artifacts and more stable narratives, enabling downstream uses such as long-form content synthesis, simulation, and creative tools for ML practitioners.
visual_elements: Schematic of sink-collapse: a short looped diagram showing generation reverting to a sink frame vs. a stable LoL-generated sequence.
Architecture diagram highlighting sink-robust attention + hierarchical memory components and how context is propagated.
Before/after example frames or short timelines comparing coherence and motion continuity over long horizons.
Line chart of coherence/quality metrics over time (baseline vs. LoL) showing reduced degradation.
paper_title: LoL: Longer than Longer, Scaling Video Generation to Hour
paper_authors: Justin Cui, Jie Wu, Ming Li, Tao Yang, Xiaojie Li
